# Trim the inline tab header: title weight token, size and horizontal padding

## Context

Operator direction 2026-09-01, after the narrow-header finding on the Workstation: rather than an actions overflow, challenge the `ui: 'inline'` tab header itself — the horizontal padding is too much, the title is too big, and it should not be bold. Users can drag the splitter for the rest.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-01T21:03:06Z, the last 30 A2A messages (all read-states), and the Knowledge Base ticket corpus; no equivalent. `#17950` (merged) introduced the inline/standalone variants; `#18020` (merged) fixed the drag proxy's density; neither touched title typography.

> **Body update 2026-09-01T22:20Z (author, PR #18048 round 1):** the weight token's fallback row below was wrong as first written — an undefined custom property makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time and the title inherits the document's weight, it does not fall back to anything. The consumption site now carries the fallback explicitly, so the row is true by construction; a fifth engine theme without tab tokens (`theme-cyberpunk`) is the case that made it matter. Found by Grace.

## The Problem

Measured on the Workstation (neo-dark theme, the "Queues" pane, header 180px wide, focus-revealed rail):

| Surface | Today |
|---|---|
| inline tab button padding | `4px 12px 3px` (`--tab-button-padding: 4px var(--sem-spacing-small) 3px`) |
| title font size | 16px (`--tab-button-text-font-size` → `--sem-typo-label-regular-fontSize` → `--core-fontsize-body`) |
| title font weight | 600 — inherited from `--button-text-font-weight` (`--core-fontweight-semibold`), because the tab header stylesheet sets a size token and no weight token |
| action cluster | 5 × 24px + 1px spacer = 121px |
| what the title gets | the tab overflow plugin caps the active tab to the usable 59px → a 36px text box → "Q…" |

"Queues" at 16px/600 needs 59px. Any one lever alone does not fit that case; the three together do: at 13px/400 the title needs ~45px, and 8px horizontal padding leaves it 44px. The rail is focus-transient, so this is about the focused state reading well, not about reserving space for it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss` paints `.neo-button-text` with `font-size: var(--tab-button-text-font-size)` only; the weight falls through to the generic button rule (`src/button/Base.scss`, `var(--button-text-font-weight)`). Every theme that sets a semibold button weight therefore sets semibold tab titles by accident.
- The inline variant's padding lives per theme in the `neo-tab-container-inline` blocks: neo themes `4px var(--sem-spacing-small) 3px`, classic themes `7px 10px 6px` (`resources/scss/theme-*/tab/Container.scss`).
- Emphasis for the active tab already has two carriers that cost no width: the indicator bar (`--tab-strip-height`) and the Workstation's full-ink `pressed` color.
- The active-tab cap is the overflow plugin's contract (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs#applySplit`), not a defect; it stays.
- **Five themes build, four declare tab tokens.** `theme-cyberpunk` is a first-class build target with no `tab/` directory: `--tab-button-text-color` and `--tab-button-text-font-size` are already undefined there and those two properties already inherit. A new tab-level `font-weight` rule at (0,3,0) outranks the button rule at (0,2,0), so without a fallback an undefined weight token would take away the one title property cyberpunk still got right.

## The Fix

1. Add `--tab-button-text-font-weight` as the tab title's weight authority: declared in the four engine theme files with today's effective value (`var(--button-text-font-weight)`, by reference), consumed in `src/tab/header/Button.scss` on `.neo-button-text` **with the button family's weight as the `var()` fallback**. No visual change for `ui: null` and `standalone`, in any theme — including one that declares no tab tokens.
2. In the inline variant blocks (all four engine themes), set the trimmed values: regular weight, a smaller size (neo themes: a new label-small step, `--core-fontsize-small` → `--sem-typo-label-small-*`; classic: the existing 11px is already small enough), and 8px horizontal padding (`--sem-spacing-xsmall` in the neo themes). The label-small step is declared as the full family/size/weight triple like the existing label steps — that is the design-token rule, so the family token is not dead weight.
3. The Workstation inherits the engine tokens; if its density wants a different step, it sets the token in its own Viewport stylesheet — no engine special-casing.
4. Screenshot receipts for operator acceptance: the "Queues" header at 180px, focused, before and after; one non-inline tab container to prove byte-identity.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tab-button-text-font-weight` (new token) | `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss` + the four theme `tab/header/Button.scss` files | sole weight authority for tab titles; inline variant overrides it to regular | absent → the button family's weight (`--button-text-font-weight`) through the consumption-site `var()` fallback; a theme with no tab tokens (cyberpunk) keeps its titles byte-identical | theme token comment | component paint spec, incl. a no-tab-tokens theme arm |
| inline variant padding + size | `resources/scss/theme-*/tab/Container.scss` inline blocks | 8px horizontal, one size step smaller | none | same | component paint spec + screenshots |

**Decision Record impact:** none (ADR 0029 does not govern tab typography).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `--tab-button-text-font-weight` token exists in all four engine themes and is the only rule deciding a tab title's weight; `ui: null` and `standalone` containers render byte-identical to before (computed size, weight, padding compared in `test/playwright/component/tab/ContainerUi.spec.mjs`), and a theme that declares no tab tokens keeps the button family's weight through the fallback.
- [ ] The inline variant renders titles at regular weight, one size step smaller than today, with 8px horizontal padding, in all four engine themes.
- [ ] On the Workstation, the "Queues" header at its default 180px shows the full title while focused with the engine rail revealed (screenshot receipt before/after).
- [ ] The drag proxy for an inline header (`#18020`) keeps the same density as the header it left.
- [ ] Operator visual acceptance on the screenshots.

## Out of Scope

- An actions overflow control for narrow headers (rejected for now: the rail is focus-transient and the splitter is the honest fix).
- The overflow plugin's active-tab cap.
- The standalone variant's geometry.
- `theme-cyberpunk`'s missing tab tokens for color and size (pre-existing: those two properties already inherit there today; this ticket only guarantees it loses nothing further).

## Avoided Traps

- Fixing the Workstation only in its own stylesheet — the leak is an engine token gap and every consumer inherits it.
- Reducing `--tab-header-action-size` to buy width — 24px is already the minimum honest hit target.
- Declaring the new token as a literal in the theme files — the identity with the button family would then hold only as of today; by reference it survives a future retune.
- Consuming the token without a fallback — a theme that never opted into tab tokens would have its titles regress silently, invisible to a four-theme matrix.
